evidence: Test suite: 1793 unit tests + 11 integration test files. Coverage is 96.13% on src/ (above 96% threshold).
Facade delegation tests (test_211_*.py) use Mock(spec=...) correctly to test that FFBBAPIClientV2 delegates to the correct sub-client. This is appropriate for facade testing.
Model tests (tests/unit/models/) cover from_dict/to_dict round-trips, edge cases, and invalid input. Comprehensive for the data layer.
Integration tests (tests/integration/) require API tokens via environment variables — they skip cleanly when tokens are absent. This is correct behavior.
No test markers distinguishing unit/integration/e2e — tox runs all tests together. The integration tests that fail without tokens cause ERROR (not FAIL) in tox output.
Test file naming convention: test_NNN_description.py with sequential numbers. The numbering implies a run order that pytest does not honor by default, potentially misleading.
Test class names: Test211FFBBAPIClientV2NewEndpoints (class number matches file number) — provides some organization but makes topic discovery hard.
examples/ and scripts/ have zero test coverage. extract_contacts.py (5000+ LOC) is entirely untested.
converter_utils.py is partially tested (91% per coverage report). The untested paths include from_uuid edge cases and some from_list branches.
No property-based tests (hypothesis) for model round-trips or converter edge cases, which would be highly effective for this domain.
Test isolation is good: all unit tests use mocks/fixtures, no external calls in unit tests.
test_strategy.issues_preventing_higher_score: examples/scripts untested (5000+ LOC extract_contacts.py), no property-based tests for data layer, test file numbering convention obscures topic organization

test_strategy.dimension_character: The library core (src/) has strong unit test coverage at 96%+ with a well-structured model testing approach. The significant gap is the complete absence of tests for examples/ and scripts/, which collectively contain 16,000+ LOC including complex business logic in extract_contacts.py. The test strategy is strong for the library but weak for the operational tooling.
test_strategy.score_rationale: Score of 52 reflects excellent library coverage (96%+) balanced against zero test coverage for 16,000 LOC of examples/scripts code that contains real business logic. The testing infrastructure quality is high, but the strategy scope is incomplete.

issues.summary: examples/ and scripts/ (~16,000 LOC total) have zero automated test coverage
evidence: examples/extract_contacts.py is 5000+ LOC with complex business logic (geo-distance calculation, HTML generation, data assembly) — entirely untested
scripts/discover_types.py is 2680 LOC with complex data processing — entirely untested
tox.ini test command runs pytest tests/ which excludes examples/ and scripts/ — no unit tests exist for these
issues.suggestion: Add unit tests for critical functions in extract_contacts.py: ContactReport.build(), _build_team_report(), _step1_geo_search_engagements() (can be tested with mocks). For scripts/, test the pure-logic functions (deduplicate helpers, phase functions). Target functions with >50 LOC or complex branching first.

issues.summary: Sequential numeric test file names (test_NNN_*.py) make topic discovery hard
evidence: test_146_error_handling_edge_cases.py, test_147_performance_resilience.py — numbers imply execution order but provide no topic signal
Finding tests for a specific model (e.g., GetOrganismeResponse) requires either grep or reading all file names
issues.suggestion: For new test files, prefer topic-based naming: test_get_organisme_response.py, test_converter_utils_dates.py. The numeric prefix convention can be maintained for existing files but should not be extended to new ones.

root_causes: test strategy focused on library code, treating examples/scripts as outside scope
